issues.detail: The Greek verb 'λεγει' (speaks/says) is used in the sense of asking or telling, but the Vietnamese translation renders it as a question ('Ngài hỏi'), whereas the Greek structure 'ποσους αρτους εχετε υπαγετε και ιδετε' (how many loaves do you have, go and see) functions more as an instruction/command combined with an inquiry. More importantly, the Vietnamese adds 'Hãy đi xem' as a separate imperative command, while in Greek it is part of the same verbal flow.
